description: This OSMRE page lists recent surface coal mining activities on federal lands that need environmental assessments or environmental impact statements under the National Environmental Policy Act before the Department of the Interior decides on a mining plan. Each project entry, split into pending and completed documents, describes the mine and its operator and links the assessments, impact statements and records of decision; examples include the Black Butte, Spring Creek and Navajo mines, the Antelope mine in Wyoming and the Freedom mine in North Dakota. It is published by the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement. Coverage is federal coal mining plans in the United States, and the page notes that under the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 assessments must be finished within one year and impact statements within two. The documents are free online; no licence is stated. Caveats: only recent active projects are listed, and abandoned mine land documents are kept in a separate oversight database. For simulation it gives planned mine expansions, production levels and environmental effects that inform coal supply and power generation scenarios and the retirement or extension of mines feeding power plants. It is related to the OSMRE national mine map repository record in this catalogue.
